## Choice 2

Recreate the graph shown below. It shows monthly homicides in Baltimore, with a reference added for the date of the arrest of Freddie Gray and color used to show colder months (November through April) versus warmer months (May through October). There is a smooth line added to help show seasonal and long-term trends in this data.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)
```



```{r}

homicides <- read.csv("/Users/sag165/Documents/RStudio/ERHS 535/HW5/data/homicide-data.csv")

homicides$city_name <- paste(homicides$city, homicides$state, sep = ", ")

#head(homicides)

baltimore_homicides <- homicides %>% 
  filter(city_name == "Baltimore, MD") %>%
  mutate(
    Date = ymd(reported_date),
    Month_Yr = format_ISO8601(Date, precision = "ym")) %>% 
    group_by(Month_Yr) %>% 
    summarise(
    homicides_total = n())


head(baltimore_homicides)

```


```{r}
ggplot(baltimore_homicides, aes(x = Month_Yr, y=homicides_total)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x= "Date", y="Monthly homicides", title="Homicides in Baltimore, MD") +
  theme_dark()
```
